name: a-chrome-row-is-dropped-and-a-cold-row-closes
description: Five chrome://settings rows survived a quit and came back as rows that answered neither a click nor their x: the cold-row opener refuses every chrome: URL, and sidebarTabClosed carries the empty id a cold row has. Two checks in one launch. First, the store carries a chrome://settings row between a live page and a cold one, and the sidebar draws only the two pages - the load dropped the row nothing could reopen. Second, the x on the cold row removes it: the census afterwards holds the live row alone. Rows are chosen by DATA (a data-url with no data-tab-id is the cold case), never by position, and the click is a DOM event on the x itself, because the sidebar layout has moved under hardcoded coordinates before.

actions.note: THE FIRST GATE. A 'cold:settings' entry here means the chrome:// row survived the load.

actions.expression: (() => { const row = [...document.querySelectorAll('[data-dropzone="tabs"] .tabrow')].find((r) => r.dataset.url && !r.dataset.tabId && !r.dataset.elsewhereTabId); if (!row) { return 'no cold row'; } const x = row.querySelector('.x'); if (!x) { return 'no x'; } x.dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', {bubbles: true, cancelable: true, view: window})); return 'clicked ' + row.dataset.url; })()

actions.note: THE SECOND GATE. The cold row still listed means its x sent nothing the browser acted on.

assertions.desc: the chrome://settings row is dropped on load, the two pages stay in order
the click landed on the cold row's own x
the x on a cold row removes it
